ea252390-7428-4717-8f42-ab7ed7cef790.summary:
Urza, Lord High Artificer is a mono-blue artifact combo commander — the #1 most popular commander on EDHREC with 20,000+ decks.

**What he does:**
1. **ETB:** Creates a Construct token that grows with your artifact count (often a 10/10+ beater)
2. **Mana engine:** Tap ANY artifact to add {U} — your Sol Rings tap twice, your 0-cost trinkets become Mox Sapphires
3. **Card advantage:** Pay {5} to shuffle and exile the top card, cast it free this turn

**How decks play him:**
- **Artifacts (14%)** — Value engine, lots of cheap artifacts, Unwinding Clock synergy
- **Combo (4%)** — Basalt Monolith + Rings of Brighthearth for infinite mana, Dramatic Reversal + Isochron Scepter
- **cEDH (3%)** — Fast mana (Mana Vault, Mox Opal, Chrome Mox), Force of Will protection, compact combo kills

**The stax trick:** Winter Orb and Static Orb only work while untapped. Tap them with Urza at end of opponent's turn — they suffer the restriction, you don't.

**Core cards:** Sol Ring, Dramatic Reversal, Basalt Monolith, Fabricate, Unwinding Clock, Isochron Scepter

**Salt score:** 2.31 — people know what's coming when they see Urza.

91c93724-437e-4382-ab4a-3821a6cf34f0.summary:
Yedora, Grave Gardener is a mono-green combo/value commander — #27 on EDHREC with 3,000+ decks.

**What she does:**
Whenever a nontoken creature you control dies, return it face-down as a Forest land. That's it — one sentence that enables ridiculous loops.

**How decks play her:**
- **Aristocrats combo** — Creatures die, become lands, sacrifice the lands with effects that untap, repeat. Life and Limb + any sac outlet = infinite deaths.
- **Morph/Manifest synergy** — Face-down creatures that die come back as lands, then you can flip them.
- **Landfall value** — Every creature death triggers landfall. Lotus Cobra makes this obscene.

**Key combos:**
- **Life and Limb + sac outlet** — All Forests are Saprolings. Yedora makes dead creatures into Forests. They're also creatures. They die. Infinite loop.
- **Ashaya + any sac outlet** — All creatures are Forests. They die, come back as Forests (which are creatures because Ashaya). Infinite.

**Core cards:** Life and Limb, Ashaya, Greater Good, Altar of Dementia, Lotus Cobra, Tireless Provisioner

**The appeal:** Mono-green combo that doesn't feel like combo — it's just lands and creatures doing weird things together.

7efd346e-9815-4934-b04a-e27b055a23fa.summary:
Wilhelt, the Rotcleaver is a Dimir zombie tribal commander — #2 on EDHREC with 22,000+ decks. The zombie precon commander that became a format staple.

**What he does:**
1. **Death replacement:** When a Zombie you control dies, if it didn't have decayed, create a 2/2 Zombie with decayed
2. **Card draw:** At the beginning of your end step, sacrifice a Zombie to draw a card

**How decks play him:**
- **Zombie tribal** — Play zombies, they die, make more zombies, draw cards. Self-sustaining engine.
- **Aristocrats** — Zombies dying creates triggers. Zombies making zombies on death doubles the triggers.
- **Combo** — Gravecrawler + any sac outlet + Wilhelt = infinite death triggers

**Why he's #2:**
- Built-in card advantage (rare for tribal commanders)
- Creates board presence from deaths (turns removal into value)
- Low mana cost (4 CMC)
- Pre-built in a precon (accessible entry point)

**Key cards:** Gravecrawler, Rooftop Storm, Undead Augur, Diregraf Captain, Corpse Harvester, Poppet Stitcher

**The loop:** Gravecrawler dies → Wilhelt makes a token → sacrifice token to draw → cast Gravecrawler from graveyard → repeat.

6de7da11-577d-4665-8b74-946285ff462c.summary:
Auntie Ool, Cursewretch is a Jund curses commander — #4 on EDHREC with 18,300+ decks.

**What she does:**
- 3/3 menace for {1}{B}{R}{G}
- Whenever a Curse enters attached to an opponent, create a Food token
- {T}, Sacrifice a Food: Return target Curse from your graveyard to the battlefield attached to an opponent

**The engine:** Play curses → make food → sacrifice food → recur curses → more food → infinite curse loop.

**How decks play her:**
- **Curse tribal** — Stack curses on opponents. Curse of Opulence, Curse of Disturbance, Curse of the Restless Dead all trigger on attack.
- **Recursion value** — Curses die to enchantment removal? Bring them back with food. They never stay gone.
- **Political manipulation** — Point curses at the threat. Incentivize attacks away from you.

**Key synergies:**
- Curses that trigger on attack point the table at one opponent
- Food from curse ETBs fuels recursion
- Jund gives access to the best curses across colors

**Core cards:** Curse of Opulence, Curse of the Restless Dead, Curse of Disturbance, Academy Manufactor, Fraying Sanity, Overwhelming Splendor

**The appeal:** Finally a dedicated curses commander. Recursive, political, and rewards a traditionally weak archetype.

ab94451f-4f1a-48b9-904b-b51965b7af56.summary:
Rocco, Cabaretti Caterer is a Naya creature toolbox commander — #12 on EDHREC with 9,500+ decks.

**What he does:**
When Rocco enters, if you cast him, search your library for a creature with mana value X or less and put it onto the battlefield. X is the amount of mana spent beyond {R}{G}{W}.

**The math:** Pay 3 for Rocco, get nothing. Pay 4, get a 1-drop. Pay 6, get a 3-drop. Pay 10, get a 7-drop.

**How decks play him:**
- **Creature toolbox** — Every game, Rocco fetches exactly what you need. Removal? Rec Sage. Ramp? Dockside. Combo? Kiki-Jiki.
- **Combo finisher** — High mana = tutor any creature combo piece directly to battlefield
- **Value beats** — Even without combo, tutoring the perfect creature every turn wins games

**Key targets:**
- **Low (1-3):** Dockside Extortionist, Esper Sentinel, Collector Ouphe
- **Mid (4-5):** Restoration Angel, Felidar Guardian, Karmic Guide
- **High (6+):** Kiki-Jiki, Craterhoof Behemoth, Avenger of Zendikar

**Core cards:** Dockside Extortionist, Kiki-Jiki, Village Bell-Ringer, Temur Sabertooth (bounce Rocco, recast)

**The appeal:** Naya gets to play like a blue deck — consistent, tutor-based game plans.

754db987-0665-4d07-8fd0-bec74fbab192.summary:
Talrand, Sky Summoner is a mono-blue spellslinger commander — #7 in mono-blue on EDHREC with 6,800+ decks.

**What he does:**
Whenever you cast an instant or sorcery spell, create a 2/2 blue Drake creature token with flying.

**That's it.** Cast spells, make drakes, win with the sky army.

**How decks play him:**
- **Counterspell tribal** — Every counter makes a drake. You're playing control and building a board.
- **Cantrip storm** — Cheap draw spells (Ponder, Preordain, Brainstorm) are now 'draw a card, make a 2/2 flyer'
- **Polymorph combo** — Drakes are the only creatures. Polymorph a drake into Tidespout Tyrant or Jin-Gitaxias.

**Why it works:**
- Mono-blue wants to hold up mana anyway
- Drakes are evasive (flying)
- Incidental army from doing what blue does

**Core cards:** Counterspell, Brainstorm, Ponder, Arcane Denial, Cyclonic Rift, Mystic Confluence

**Budget appeal:** The deck is literally 'instants and sorceries you own.' Works at any budget level.

56604577-fc23-4e96-85b1-6ed586c60338.summary:
Ruric Thar, the Unbowed is a Gruul anti-spell beatdown commander — #14 in Gruul on EDHREC with 6,700+ decks.

**What he does:**
- Vigilance, reach, must attack each turn
- **Whenever a player casts a noncreature spell, Ruric Thar deals 6 damage to that player**

**The rule:** Everyone takes 6 when they cast noncreature spells. Including you. So don't cast noncreature spells.

**How decks play him:**
- **Creature-only Gruul** — 40+ creatures, very few instants/sorceries. Creature-based ramp, removal, draw.
- **Stax** — Opponents can't play their decks without eating 6 damage per spell
- **Beatdown** — 6/6 vigilance reach that must attack. He's already a clock.

**Build constraint:** The deck builds itself by restriction. If it's not a creature or land, you probably don't want it.

**Key cards:** Dockside Extortionist, Collector Ouphe, Manglehorn, Kogla, Reclamation Sage, Beast Whisperer

**The appeal:** Punishes spell-heavy decks (combo, control) while Gruul does what Gruul does — big creatures, turn sideways.

2975d418-df52-43fa-abf9-cb632ef72321.summary:
Arcades, the Strategist is a Bant defender tribal commander — #2 in Bant on EDHREC with 22,700+ decks.

**What he does:**
1. **Defender creatures can attack as though they didn't have defender**
2. **Creatures you control with defender deal damage equal to their toughness**
3. **Whenever a creature with defender enters, draw a card**

**The twist:** Your 0/5 walls become 5/5 attackers that draw cards. Wall of Omens is now a 0-mana 4/4 that draws 2 cards.

**How decks play him:**
- **Wall beatdown** — High toughness = high damage. Charix is a 17/17 for 4 mana.
- **Card advantage engine** — Every defender draws. Flood the board, draw your deck.
- **Combo** — Infinite mana with Axebane Guardian + enough defenders. High Alert as backup Arcades.

**Key cards:** Wall of Omens, Wall of Blossoms, Axebane Guardian, Overgrown Battlement, High Alert, Assault Formation

**Budget appeal:** Walls are cheap. A $30 Arcades deck performs like a $300 deck because the creatures cost pennies.

**The appeal:** Turns unplayable draft chaff into a legitimate strategy. Big butts matter.

9e3f49b9-cdfd-4190-aef7-f10fa2c25fed.summary:
Hakbal of the Surging Soul is a Simic merfolk tribal commander — #1 on EDHREC with 24,800+ decks (precon popularity).

**What he does:**
Whenever you attack, explore with Hakbal. Then you may put a land from your hand onto the battlefield. If you explored this way and Hakbal is tapped, merfolk you control can't be blocked this turn.

**The combo:** Attack → explore (draw/grow) → drop extra land → merfolk unblockable.

**How decks play him:**
- **Merfolk tribal** — Lords, unblockable, go wide
- **Explore synergy** — Explore multiple times per turn, grow creatures, dig for lands
- **Landfall backup** — Extra land drops trigger landfall incidentally

**Key synergies:**
- Attack triggers + extra combat = multiple explores
- Explore with big library = grow Hakbal huge
- Unblockable merfolk = reliable damage

**Core cards:** Deeproot Pilgrimage, Svyelun, Merrow Reejerey, Kopala, Enter the Unknown, Nautical Palisade

**The appeal:** Precon commander that's genuinely strong. Tribal + ramp + card advantage + evasion in one package.

ff01d14d-4bff-4755-9d29-aa60cc3fa36d.summary:
The Scarab God is a Dimir zombie reanimator commander — #7 in Dimir on EDHREC with 14,000+ decks.

**What he does:**
1. **Upkeep:** Scry X, opponents lose X life, you gain X life (X = zombies you control)
2. **Activate {2}{U}{B}:** Exile a creature from any graveyard, create a 4/4 zombie token copy
3. **When TSG dies:** Return to hand at next end step (extremely hard to remove permanently)

**How decks play him:**
- **Graveyard theft** — Mill opponents, steal their best creatures as 4/4 zombie copies
- **Zombie tribal** — The upkeep trigger scales with zombie count. Lots of zombies = lots of drain + scry
- **Control/value** — Doesn't need to attack or even have a board. Just slowly drain and steal.

**Why he's resilient:**
- Returns to hand on death (can't be tucked easily)
- Doesn't need to untap (upkeep trigger happens regardless)
- Creatures you steal don't need to survive (already zombies)

**Core cards:** Undead Augur, Zombie Master, Gravecrawler, Altar of Dementia, Mesmeric Orb, Rooftop Storm

**The appeal:** Inevitability. Even if you answer TSG, he comes back. Even if you wipe the board, he steals from graveyards.

b2550151-59d5-4781-8a07-782d2ecfa1b8.summary:
Pantlaza, Sun-Favored is a Naya dinosaur tribal commander — #1 on EDHREC with 35,800+ decks (Lost Caverns precon effect).

**What he does:**
Whenever Pantlaza or another Dinosaur enters, you discover X (X = that dino's toughness).

**Discover reminder:** Exile cards from library until you hit a nonland with mana value X or less. Cast it free or put it in hand.

**How decks play him:**
- **Dinosaur cascade** — Big dinos = big discovers. Ghalta discovers 12. Zetalpa discovers 8.
- **Value engine** — Every dino is a dino + a free spell. Carnage Tyrant discovers 5 AND you get Carnage Tyrant.
- **Combo potential** — Discover into haste enablers, extra combat, more dinos, repeat.

**Key math:**
- Pantlaza himself discovers 4 when he enters (his toughness)
- Etali discovers 6. Regisaur Alpha discovers 4. Polyraptor discovers 5.

**Core cards:** Etali, Ghalta, Regisaur Alpha, Wayward Swordtooth, Gishath, Xenagos

**The appeal:** Dinosaurs were already fun. Now every dinosaur is two spells. Value pile that hits hard.

773e1927-04cb-4288-9389-8add1607cc07.summary:
The First Sliver is a 5-color sliver tribal commander — #9 on EDHREC with 19,400+ decks.

**What he does:**
- Cascade (when cast, exile cards until you hit a cheaper nonland, cast it free)
- **Sliver spells you cast have cascade**

**The avalanche:** Cast a sliver → cascade into another sliver → that sliver cascades → repeat until you hit a 0-cost.

**How decks play him:**
- **Sliver tribal** — Lords, keyword soup, overwhelming board presence
- **Cascade value** — Every sliver is 2+ slivers. Board fills fast.
- **Combo** — Cascade into specific pieces. Lavadome into Blur Sliver into Cloudshredder.

**The cascade chain:**
- Cast 5-drop sliver → cascade into 4-drop → cascade into 3-drop → cascade into 2-drop → cascade into 1-drop
- One spell becomes five slivers

**Key slivers:** Cloudshredder (haste/flying), Harmonic (Rec Sage), Bonescythe (double strike), Galerider (flying), Manaweft (mana)

**The appeal:** Most explosive sliver commander. Other sliver legends need setup; First Sliver snowballs immediately.

**Salt warning:** Cascade is random but often feels unfair. Slivers are already polarizing.

f6002633-3fb1-4764-ab58-e4d93b00ab61.summary:
Hearthhull, the Worldseed is a Jund lands/tokens commander — #1 on EDHREC with 29,700+ decks (Foundations Jumpstart effect).

**What it does:**
1. **Landfall:** Whenever a land enters, create a 1/1 green Elemental creature token
2. **Sacrifice 3 creatures:** Search your library for a basic land and put it onto the battlefield

**The engine:** Lands make tokens. Tokens become lands. Lands make more tokens. Self-sustaining value loop.

**How decks play it:**
- **Landfall aggro** — Every land drop is also a creature. Fetch lands are two tokens.
- **Aristocrats** — Sacrifice fodder that replaces itself with more fodder
- **Lands matter** — Ramp hard, abuse landfall triggers, Scute Swarm goes infinite

**Key synergies:**
- **Fetch lands:** Crack a fetch = 2 landfall triggers = 2 tokens
- **Scute Swarm:** 6+ lands means each land makes Scute copies, which make more tokens
- **Tireless Provisioner/Lotus Cobra:** Landfall for mana, sac tokens for more lands, mana explosion

**Core cards:** Scute Swarm, Tireless Provisioner, Lotus Cobra, Fecundity, Zuran Orb, Ramunap Excavator

**The appeal:** Jund doing Jund things — value, recursion, sacrifice — but lands are the engine instead of creatures.

d9a3e5cb-6472-48ce-aac1-165536e72c77.summary:
Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER is a mono-black voltron/reanimator commander — 28,700+ decks (Final Fantasy crossover hype).

**What he does (front face):**
- 4/4 flying, lifelink for {2}{B}{B}
- Whenever Sephiroth deals combat damage to a player, transform him

**What he does (back face - One-Winged Angel):**
- 7/7 flying, lifelink, indestructible
- When he transforms, each opponent sacrifices a creature
- At end of combat, if he dealt combat damage, you may return a creature from your graveyard to the battlefield

**The game plan:** Land one hit, flip to 7/7 indestructible, opponents sacrifice, you reanimate. Repeat.

**How decks play him:**
- **Voltron** — Equipment and auras to ensure that first hit connects. Swiftfoot Boots, Whispersilk Cloak
- **Reanimator** — Stock graveyard, flip Sephiroth, bring back bombs for free every combat
- **Aristocrats backup** — Opponents sacrificing + you reanimating = value asymmetry

**Key cards:** Swiftfoot Boots, Lightning Greaves, Reanimate, Entomb, Grave Titan, Sheoldred

**The appeal:** Final Fantasy villain as a commander. Transforms like a boss fight. Mono-black gets voltron that's actually good.

1ccfa07f-14d8-4775-98ae-a9f66d1017f6.summary:
MacCready, Lamplight Mayor is an Orzhov tokens/sacrifice commander — #51 on EDHREC with 2,100+ decks (Fallout crossover).

**What he does:**
- Whenever another creature you control dies, create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token
- Sacrifice a creature: Target creature gains deathtouch until end of turn

**The loop:** Creatures die → make tokens → sacrifice tokens → more creatures die → more tokens.

**How decks play him:**
- **Aristocrats engine** — Deaths make tokens. Tokens are sacrifice fodder. Blood Artist drains, Pitiless Plunderer makes treasures.
- **Go-wide aggro** — Incidental army from creatures dying. Board wipes that kill your stuff leave you with an army.
- **Political removal** — Give anything deathtouch at instant speed. Opponents think twice about attacking.

**Key synergies:**
- Board wipes that hit your creatures = mass token generation
- Deathtouch on any creature makes blocking/attacking awkward for opponents
- Token doublers (Anointed Procession) double the death triggers

**Core cards:** Blood Artist, Pitiless Plunderer, Anointed Procession, Skullclamp, Grave Pact, Teysa Karlov

**The appeal:** Fallout flavor meets classic Orzhov aristocrats. Resilient to removal — deaths fuel the engine.

11c7f6db-0003-4728-868c-ed5b83813eee.summary:
Zurgo Stormrender is a Mardu equipment/voltron commander — #6 on EDHREC with 20,200+ decks.

**What he does:**
- 3/4 haste for {1}{R}{W}{B}
- Whenever Zurgo attacks, create a colorless Equipment artifact token (Sword of the Khans)
- Sword of the Khans: Equipped creature gets +2/+0 and has 'Whenever this creature deals combat damage, draw a card'

**The engine:** Attack → make equipment → equip Zurgo → attack again → more equipment → bigger Zurgo → more cards.

**How decks play him:**
- **Equipment voltron** — Self-equipping commander. Every attack makes him bigger and draws cards.
- **Go-tall aggro** — Haste means he hits immediately. Equipment tokens stack fast.
- **Equipment synergies** — Puresteel Paladin, Sram, Sigarda's Aid all trigger off free equipment

**Why he's popular:**
- Built-in card advantage (combat damage → draw)
- Self-sustaining (makes his own equipment)
- Haste (immediate pressure)
- Mardu has the best equipment support

**Core cards:** Puresteel Paladin, Sram, Sigarda's Aid, Sword of Feast and Famine, Colossus Hammer, Brass Squire

**The appeal:** Voltron that doesn't run out of gas. Equipment commander that makes his own equipment.

d5a9a848-1169-4f0f-a61b-cfbf2eb822d6.summary:
Ureni of the Unwritten is a Temur typal/tribal commander — #4 on EDHREC with 21,100+ decks.

**What she does:**
- 4/4 for {2}{G}{U}{R}
- At the beginning of combat, look at the top 8 cards. You may put a creature from among them that shares a type with Ureni onto the battlefield. It gains haste.
- When that creature enters, Ureni gains all creature types until end of turn.

**The trick:** Put a creature into play → Ureni gains its types → next combat, Ureni matches MORE types → hit bigger creatures.

**How decks play her:**
- **Big creature tribal** — Eldrazi, Dragons, Dinosaurs. Ureni cheats them into play.
- **Typal soup** — Mix creature types. Ureni eventually matches everything.
- **Top-deck manipulation** — Scroll Rack, Sensei's Divining Top, Worldly Tutor to guarantee hits

**Key synergies:**
- Changelings (all creature types) guarantee Ureni matches everything
- Extra combats = multiple Ureni triggers per turn
- Haste on cheated creatures = immediate value

**Core cards:** Morophon, The World Tree, Maskwood Nexus, Scroll Rack, Sensei's Divining Top, Selvala's Stampede

**The appeal:** Cheats expensive creatures into play. Temur doing Temur things — big stuff, fast, with card selection.
